features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed frontmatter `model:` on custom commands and skills being ignored in interactive sessions
features.description: A skill's or command's frontmatter `model:` was silently ignored in interactive sessions; it now applies.
features.ork_disposition_note: Largest single behaviour change in this wave for ork. VERIFIED 39 of ork's skills declare a model pin: `grep -rl '^model:' src/skills/*/SKILL.md | wc -l` = 39 (sampled: analytics=haiku, assess=sonnet, audit-full=opus, auto=sonnet, brainstorm=sonnet). Before 2.1.259 every one of those pins was inert in an interactive session, so a skill authored to run on haiku ran on whatever the session used. Nothing to change in ork: the pins were already correct and now take effect. Users below the fix keep the old behaviour, which is why ork's floor (2.1.251) still cannot assume it.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed auto mode running a turn on a model it doesn't support when a command or skill's frontmatter `model:` named one; the turn now keeps the session model
features.description: Auto mode no longer switches to a frontmatter-named model it cannot support; it keeps the session model instead.
features.ork_disposition_note: Paired with the fix above and bounds it. ork's 39 pinned skills name only opus, sonnet and haiku (`grep -rh '^model:' src/skills/*/SKILL.md | sort -u`), all of which auto mode supports, so ork never triggered the unsupported branch. Free.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed concurrent sessions silently reverting each other's `~/.claude.json` changes
features.description: Concurrent sessions no longer clobber each other's ~/.claude.json; workspace trust and MCP/project state survive many parallel sessions.
features.ork_disposition_note: Directly relevant to how this estate is actually run: ListAgents reported 17 peer sessions (4 live interactive) while this lane was open, which is exactly the condition that produced the silent revert. ork ships no fix of its own for it and never could; the shared-state hazard it documents in the worktree rules is narrower (working tree, index, node_modules) than the ~/.claude.json class this closes. Free upside, no ork change.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed blocking Stop hooks causing the turn after a block to lose the model's reasoning from that turn and, on some models, miss the prompt cache
features.description: A blocking Stop hook no longer costs the next turn its reasoning and a prompt-cache hit.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork registers 8 Stop hooks (`ls src/hooks/src/stop/`: goal-tracker, handoff-writer, ledger-cleanup, security-scan-aggregator, session-heartbeat-finalizer, session-summary, stop-failure-handler, task-completion-check). VERIFIED none of them blocks: `grep -rn 'process.exit|decision|continue: false|block' src/hooks/src/stop/*.ts` returns only comments and unrelated identifiers (goal-tracker.ts:23 states the contract outright, 'Async: telemetry write only, must not block Stop'), and all Stop entries in src/hooks/hooks.json carry `async: true`. So ork never paid this cost and gains nothing measurable; the fix matters for users who add their own blocking Stop hook on top of ork.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed worktree isolation refusing hook-created worktrees on machines where `git rev-parse` fails with a message other than "not a git repository"
features.description: Worktree isolation no longer refuses a hook-created worktree when git rev-parse fails with an unexpected message.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork has both halves of this surface: 25 agents declare `isolation: worktree` (`grep -rl 'isolation: *worktree' src/agents/*.md | wc -l` = 25) and a hook manages worktree lifecycle (`src/hooks/src/lifecycle/sweep-stale-worktrees.ts`, written for #1884). The refusal was environment-dependent, so it was never reproducible here; free upside.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed worktree-isolated sessions refusing common Bash loops, xargs pipelines and launcher-wrapped commands that cannot reach the main checkout
features.description: Worktree-isolated sessions stop refusing Bash loops, xargs pipelines and launcher-wrapped commands.
features.ork_disposition_note: Second helping of the same free upgrade already recorded for the 25 isolation:worktree agents in the 2.1.252-257 triage. No ork change.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added `--json` to `claude plugin validate` for a machine-readable validation report
features.description: claude plugin validate gains --json for a machine-readable report.
features.ork_disposition_note: Actionable and small. ork already runs the command in CI at `.github/workflows/plugin-validation.yml:347`, but consumes only its exit code: `claude plugin validate ./plugins/ork 2>&1 || { echo "::warning::claude plugin validate reported issues"; exit 1; }`. A red run therefore says 'reported issues' and nothing about which. With --json the workflow could name the failing entries in the annotation. Deferred rather than adopted because it must not run below ork's floor (2.1.251) without a version guard, and the step already installs an unpinned CC.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added `--permission-prompts none` for unattended headless hosts
features.description: New --permission-prompts none denies anything that would prompt, while the active permission mode keeps deciding.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork has 7 headless workflows plus eval scripts driving `claude -p` (labs-version-watch, plugin-validation, ci-sentinel, claude-health, claude-release-watch, skill-eval, claude-triage; tests/evals/scripts/run-trigger-eval.sh and others). Today an unexpected prompt in those hosts hangs until the job timeout. The flag converts that into an immediate deny, which is the behaviour the workflows already want. Deferred for the same floor-guard reason as --json.

features.reference_changelog_line: Changed `allowedMcpServers` to govern only servers users add: a literal `managed-mcp.json` server your allowlist used to filter out now loads on upgrade; use `deniedMcpServers` to keep it off
features.description: allowedMcpServers now governs only user-added servers; managed-mcp.json entries it used to filter out now load.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork documents allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers enforcement in four places (`plugins/ork/skills/mcp-patterns/SKILL.md:177`, `configure/references/mcp-config.md:348`, `configure/SKILL.md:132`, `security-patterns/SKILL.md:296` and `:378`), all framed as an org-wide allowlist that filters every server. That framing is now wrong for managed entries: on upgrade, a managed-mcp.json server an allowlist used to exclude starts loading. A security doc that overstates what an allowlist covers is the kind of claim worth correcting, so this gets a doc note rather than a noop.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added `managedMcpServers` managed setting
features.description: Organizations can push HTTP/SSE MCP servers to every user via a managed setting; command-based entries are skipped.
features.ork_disposition_note: Enterprise managed-settings surface. ork ships no managed settings and cannot: managed settings are machine or org scoped, and ork's own plugin settings file is inert for everything except `agent` and `subagentStatusLine`. Nothing for ork to do beyond the mcp-config note already covering the family.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed managed settings silently going unenforced when the managed-settings file, a drop-in, the MDM plist, or the HKLM value cannot be parsed
features.description: Unparseable managed settings now stop Claude Code from starting, naming the source, instead of silently disabling enforcement.
features.ork_disposition_note: Same failure class ork already documents at `security-patterns/SKILL.md:296` for CC 2.1.166 (one invalid entry silently voiding the rest). This closes the remaining parse-level variant by refusing to start. Free; the existing note stays accurate.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed Bash `Read()` deny rules not covering files given as option values, `git diff`/`git grep` file operands, or `cd DIR && cat FILE` compounds
features.description: Read() deny rules were extended over Bash option values, git file operands and cd-compounds.
features.ork_disposition_note: Do not adopt: 2.1.260 REVERTED this one release later ('it denied `npm run build` under a `Read(./**/build/**)` rule in every mode and made `cd … && grep` prompt even in auto mode'). Net effect across the wave is zero. Recorded so a future reader does not re-adopt a reverted behaviour from the 2.1.259 snapshot alone.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added recognition of `glab mr create/merge/close/reopen/note/update`
features.description: GitLab merge requests now render as MR !N in the collapsed tool summary and refresh the footer MR badge.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork is GitHub-only: `github-operations` and every workflow use `gh`, and no ork file invokes `glab`. Nothing to adopt.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed managed `skillOverrides` entries keyed on a bundled skill's alias (e.g. `checkup` for `/doctor`) not applying, and `Skill(name)` deny rules not covering a nested skill listed as `<dir>:name`
features.description: Skill(name) deny rules now cover a nested skill addressed as <dir>:name, and skillOverrides keyed on an alias apply.
features.ork_disposition_note: Every user-facing ork skill IS a `<dir>:name` skill: all 106 surface as `/ork:<skillname>` (CLAUDE.md, Plugin Architecture). Before 2.1.260 an operator who wrote `Skill(audit-full)` to deny one of them was not actually denying anything, because the skill is listed as `ork:audit-full`. That is a silent-permission-gap of exactly the class ork's own security docs warn about, and it argues for spelling the prefixed form in `configure`. Doc-level, since ork ships no Skill() deny rules of its own.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` on macOS hiding the user's git config from sandboxed git and hiding a worktree-isolated sub-agent's own checkout
features.description: blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories no longer hides git config from sandboxed git, nor a worktree-isolated subagent's own checkout.
features.ork_disposition_note: Hits ork's most-used isolation path: 25 agents declare `isolation: worktree`, and `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` is already documented in `configure` (adopted in the 2.1.252-257 wave). A subagent that cannot read its OWN checkout is the worst shape of this bug, because the failure reads as a missing file rather than a permission denial. Free at 2.1.260; the configure note stays correct.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed Bash permission checks auto-approving zsh commands that hide a command substitution in a REPORTTIME, REPORTMEMORY or DIRSTACKSIZE assignment; these now prompt for approval
features.description: Command substitution hidden in a zsh REPORTTIME/REPORTMEMORY/DIRSTACKSIZE assignment no longer auto-approves.
features.ork_disposition_note: A real permission-bypass class, and one ork's own suite did not cover: `ls tests/security/` includes test-command-injection.sh, test-compound-commands.sh and test-line-continuation-bypass.sh, none of which probes a zsh numeric-assignment carrier. It also lands on this machine's actual shell (`Shell: zsh`). Worth a line in security-patterns; a matching probe in tests/security is the natural follow-up but is a code change, not a triage row.

features.reference_changelog_line: Removed the one-hour time limit on background commands started by subagents; they now run until they exit or are stopped, matching the main session
features.description: Background commands started by subagents no longer die at one hour.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork fans work out to subagents that start long-running background commands (test suites, builds, browser sessions), and a silent one-hour ceiling is the kind of limit that reads as a hung agent rather than a kill. Free upside, no ork change; worth knowing when a long agent run previously 'stalled' near the hour mark.

features.reference_changelog_line: Changed commands typed at the `!` bash-mode prompt to run outside the sandbox even when strict sandbox mode (`sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`) is on, like typing into your own terminal
features.description: The ! bash-mode prompt now runs outside the sandbox even under strict sandbox mode.
features.ork_disposition_note: A deliberate hole in a setting whose name promises the opposite: `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` no longer covers the `!` prompt. It is defensible (the operator typed it themselves) but anyone reading the setting as a hard boundary is now wrong, so it belongs in the sandbox prose rather than left implicit.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added a likely cause for prompt-cache misses (e.g. tool definitions or system prompt changed, idle past the TTL) to `/cost` and the status line's `prompt_cache` field
features.description: /cost and the status line's prompt_cache field now name a likely cause for a cache miss.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork's cost story is cache-dominated (the estate's measured cache-read to fresh-input ratio is roughly 386:1), and a plugin that injects tool definitions and a system prompt is itself a plausible cache-miss cause. A native per-miss reason is strictly better than inferring it from token counts, which is what ork's analytics currently does. Doc note in analytics.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed `Edit`/`Write`/`Read` permission rules whose path contains parentheses being dropped as invalid or ignored by the Bash sandbox, which left "read-only" folders writable
features.description: Permission rules whose path contains parentheses are no longer dropped as invalid or ignored by the Bash sandbox.
features.ork_disposition_note: Noop for ork's shipped rules, for two independent reasons. VERIFIED none of the 25 deny rules in src/settings/ork.settings.json contains a parenthesis inside the path (they are plain forms such as `Read(~/.ssh/**)`, `Bash(rm -rf /)`, `Bash(find *-delete*)`). And ork's plugin settings `permissions` block is discarded by CC regardless: only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` are read from a plugin settings file. Users writing their own parenthesised rules get the fix.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed one file permission rule with an uncompilable pattern (e.g. an unclosed `[`) making every file edit fail with `Invalid regular expression`
features.description: A single uncompilable permission pattern no longer breaks every file edit; the deny rule now guards the literal path it spells.
features.ork_disposition_note: Blast radius out of all proportion to the typo: one unclosed bracket anywhere in a user's rules broke every edit in the session. Free; ork ships no bracket patterns (see the rule list above).

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed `model: fable` agents ignoring the `[1m]` tag on an `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` pin and silently running with a 200K context window
features.description: model: fable agents now honour the [1m] tag on an ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL pin instead of silently using 200K.
features.ork_disposition_note: VERIFIED no ork agent pins fable: `grep -rh '^model:' src/agents/*.md | sort | uniq -c` gives 23 sonnet, 6 opus, 4 inherit, 3 haiku and nothing else. ork mentions fable only in prose (`auto`, `verify`, `configure/references/cc-version-settings.md`) and deliberately keeps fable behind a consent hook rather than a pin. Silent context-window downgrade is exactly the failure that hook exists to avoid, so the fix is welcome but unexercised here.

features.reference_changelog_line: Reverted the 2.1.259 change applying `Read()` deny rules to Bash arguments
features.description: The 2.1.259 extension of Read() deny rules over Bash arguments was reverted after it denied npm run build and made cd-compounds prompt in auto mode.
features.ork_disposition_note: The other half of `bash_read_deny_option_values_259`. Worth reading as a warning about ork's own guard design: a path-shaped deny rule applied to command TEXT catches builds and greps that were never reading a secret. ork has hit the same class in its own hooks.

features.reference_changelog_line: Changed permission rules with text after the closing parenthesis (e.g. `Bash(ls) x`), which never matched anything, to be reported as invalid settings instead of being silently ignored
features.description: A permission rule with trailing text after the closing parenthesis is now reported invalid instead of silently ignored.
features.ork_disposition_note: VERIFIED no rule in src/settings/ork.settings.json has text after the closing parenthesis (all 30 allow+deny entries end at `)` or are bare tool names such as `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`). A silently-ignored rule that now speaks up is the right direction; nothing to change.

features.reference_changelog_line: Improved structured output: Workflow `agent({schema})` rejects a JSON Schema that can never be satisfied up front, and retry-cap errors now include the last validation failure
features.description: Workflow agent({schema}) rejects an unsatisfiable JSON Schema up front; retry-cap errors name the last validation failure.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork's fan-out skills pass schemas to Workflow agents (audit-full-mapreduce, skill-fitness). Failing at definition time instead of after N burned retries is a straight win on both latency and spend. Free.

features.reference_changelog_line: Improved auto-compact for 1M-context models: Opus and Fable sessions now compact shortly before the 1M-token limit, and recovery compaction on very large contexts no longer times out at 10 minutes
features.description: 1M-context Opus and Fable sessions compact near the real limit, and recovery compaction no longer times out.
features.ork_disposition_note: Applies to the sessions ork development actually runs in (this lane is Opus with a 1M window). Free.

features.reference_changelog_line: Improved deleting a background session whose worktree has unpushed commits: the message now names the branch and commit count, and deleting again discards the worktree
features.description: Deleting a background session with unpushed commits names the branch and commit count before discarding.
features.ork_disposition_note: Guards the exact loss ork's worktree rules exist to prevent, and does it natively. Free.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added `/reload-plugins` to headless sessions, so it appears in the Claude Code Desktop and SDK command lists
features.description: /reload-plugins is now available in headless sessions and listed in Desktop and SDK command lists.
features.ork_disposition_note: Relevant to ork's plugin-development loop (edit src, rebuild, reload) now that the headless hosts can reload too. No ork change; worth knowing when debugging a stale plugin in a `claude -p` host.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added a diff panel that opens beside the conversation in fullscreen mode and shows your uncommitted changes as Claude edits; toggle it with `/diff`
features.description: A /diff panel shows uncommitted changes beside the conversation in fullscreen mode.
features.ork_disposition_note: Native UI, no plugin surface. Noted because it overlaps what ork's stop-uncommitted-check hook nags about: the operator can now see the same uncommitted state continuously instead of at Stop.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added `/skill-doctor` to show which loaded skills go unused and what they cost in context, so you can prune them
features.description: New /skill-doctor reports which loaded skills go unused and what they cost in context.
features.ork_disposition_note: Highest-value row of the wave for ork specifically. ork ships 106 skills in one plugin and CLAUDE.md already treats per-session token cost as a headline number (`claude plugin details ork`). `/skill-doctor` answers the unused-and-what-does-it-cost question natively, per session, on the real loaded set, which is strictly better evidence than ork's own two attempts at it: `audit-activation` reads spawn telemetry and `skill-fitness` scores a rubric, neither measures context cost. VERIFIED ork has no reference to it yet: `grep -rn 'skill-doctor' src shared docs/site/content` hits only the 2.1.261 snapshot. This is a doc adoption now and a candidate to make audit-activation cite /skill-doctor rather than approximate it.

features.reference_changelog_line: Changed auto mode to treat a link that packs content into a public diagram renderer's URL as an upload to that site: no longer auto-approved unless you asked for it
features.description: Auto mode treats a URL that packs content into a public diagram renderer as an upload to that site, so it is no longer auto-approved.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork contains exactly one call site of this shape and it is latent, not live. VERIFIED `src/hooks/src/lib/decision-history.ts:803-822` defines `validateMermaidViaAPI`, which base64-encodes caller-supplied Mermaid and fetches `https://mermaid.ink/svg/${base64}`, which is precisely 'packs content into a public diagram renderer's URL'. VERIFIED it is dead: `grep -rn 'validateMermaidViaAPI' src` finds the definition and its own unit test and no other caller, so nothing in ork is broken by this change today. Recorded as watch, not noop, because the function is exported and its only guard is a catch that returns true; if it is ever wired into a hook path it will need explicit approval in auto mode, and it would be silently shipping decision text to a third-party host either way. The right follow-up is to delete it or gate it, which is a code change and out of scope for a triage row.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added `bashOutputMaxChars` and `taskOutputMaxChars` settings to raise how much command and background-task output Claude receives inline before it is saved to a file, up to 128K characters
features.description: New bashOutputMaxChars and taskOutputMaxChars settings raise the inline output ceiling to 128K characters before spill-to-file.
features.ork_disposition_note: Directly governs a behaviour ork sessions hit constantly: a large tool result is truncated to a persisted-output file (this lane hit it once, at 31KB). Both settings belong in `configure`'s settings reference. VERIFIED ork documents neither today: `grep -rniE 'bashOutputMaxChars|taskOutputMaxChars|maxOutputChars' src shared docs/site/content` hits only the 2.1.261 snapshot. Raising the ceiling trades context spend for fewer round-trips, so the doc note should say that rather than recommend a value.

features.reference_changelog_line: Changed the prompt's word-editing keys to match Bash: Ctrl+W deletes back to whitespace, Alt+F and Alt+D stop at word end, punctuation separates words; `keybindingFlavor` no longer has any effect
features.description: Bash-style word editing is now unconditional and the keybindingFlavor setting is inert.
features.ork_disposition_note: This one makes an existing ork claim STALE, which is why it is an adoption and not a noop. ork adopted `keybindingFlavor` across two earlier waves (snapshots 2.1.238 introduced it, 2.1.239 extended it) and carries the resulting note in `docs/site/lib/generated/cc-adoption-data.ts:1340`: 'New keybindingFlavor settings key (classic|readline) changes prompt editing-key semantics; operator-scope settings references should list it.' A settings reference that lists a key CC no longer reads is worse than no note. The generated file derives from the gaps feed, so the correction belongs here and propagates on rebuild.

features.reference_changelog_line: Improved the dangerous-`rm` safety prompt to also catch `rm -rf` on positional parameters and inside double-quoted `sh -c` scripts
features.description: The dangerous-rm prompt now catches rm -rf on positional parameters and inside double-quoted sh -c scripts.
features.ork_disposition_note: Closes two carriers that ork's own deny rules structurally cannot see. VERIFIED ork ships 9 literal `rm -rf` deny rules in src/settings/ork.settings.json (`Bash(rm -rf /)`, `Bash(rm -rf ~)`, `Bash(rm -rf .)`, the /private/* pair set), all of which match command TEXT and therefore miss `rm -rf "$1"` and `sh -c "rm -rf …"` entirely; those rules are also discarded because CC reads only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` from a plugin settings file. So the native prompt is the only thing that ever covered this, and it now covers more. Free.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed in-process agent-team teammates re-sending their first-turn tool and skill announcements on the second turn, which changed the request prefix and missed the prompt cache
features.description: In-process teammates no longer re-send first-turn tool and skill announcements, which was changing the request prefix and missing the prompt cache.
features.ork_disposition_note: A prefix change on turn 2 is the most expensive shape of cache miss for a plugin like ork, because the announcement it re-sent is proportional to the loaded tool and skill surface, and ork's is large (106 skills, 36 agents). Every ork skill that fans out to in-process teammates paid it. Free, and it should show up as a measurable drop in fresh-input tokens on multi-turn fan-outs.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed resuming a session losing hook output and other context around parallel tool calls, which changed the resumed request
features.description: Resuming a session no longer drops hook output and other context around parallel tool calls.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork is hook-dense and its hooks speak by injecting context (nudges, rule-precedence banners, guard warnings), so a resume that drops hook output silently removes guardrails from the resumed session. Nothing to change in ork; the fix restores an assumption ork's hook design already made.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added an "Organization policy" line to `/status` and `claude doctor` that says why your organization's policy could not be loaded, such as a proxy not passing the endpoint through
features.description: /status and claude doctor now explain why an organization policy could not be loaded.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork's `doctor` skill is the diagnostic front door and already reconciles CC-native signals; a native policy-load failure line is one more thing it should point at rather than reimplement. Small doc note.

features.reference_changelog_line: Added `--append-subagent-system-prompt-file` to read the subagent system prompt from a file, for prompts too large to pass on the command line
features.description: New --append-subagent-system-prompt-file reads a subagent system prompt from a file.
features.ork_disposition_note: Fits ork's headless eval harness, where subagent prompts are assembled and passed on the command line (tests/evals/scripts, bare-eval). A file avoids both the argv ceiling and the shell-quoting hazards this repo's own rules warn about. Deferred: it needs a floor guard, and the eval harness is not currently blocked by prompt size.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed `SendMessage` to an offline Remote Control session on another machine reading as delivered; the result now says delivery is queued until that machine reconnects
features.description: SendMessage to an offline Remote Control session now reports queued delivery instead of success.
features.ork_disposition_note: A success string that meant nothing had been delivered, which is the exact false-signal class ork's verification rules exist to catch. Relevant here in practice: ListAgents in this lane listed 13 offline Remote Control peers alongside 4 live ones, so a cross-session handoff could easily have addressed one. Free.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed plugin install hints from CLIs run in background Bash commands: they are now detected, and the raw `<claude-code-hint>` tag no longer leaks into the conversation
features.description: Plugin install hints from background Bash commands are detected and the raw tag no longer leaks into the conversation.
features.ork_disposition_note: Plugin-adjacent and free. ork runs CLIs in background Bash commands from hooks and skills; a leaked raw tag is cosmetic but reads as corrupted output.

features.reference_changelog_line: Changed `/context` token counting to use a local estimate when the token-counting API is unavailable, instead of extra small-model requests
features.description: /context falls back to a local token estimate instead of issuing extra small-model requests.
features.ork_disposition_note: Removes a hidden spend path behind a diagnostic command. Free; worth knowing when reconciling ork's analytics cost figures against /context.

features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed cloud sessions discarding a plugin synced from claude.ai when managed settings force-enable it in `enabledPlugins`, then falling back to a marketplace clone that could fail
features.description: Cloud sessions no longer discard a claude.ai-synced plugin that managed settings force-enable, then fail on a marketplace clone.
features.ork_disposition_note: ork is distributed through a marketplace, so the failing fallback path is one its users can land on. ork itself sets no managed `enabledPlugins`. Free.

features.description: Claude Code launches again on macOS 12 (Monterey); the regression came in with 2.1.255, a build that never got a CHANGELOG entry.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed Claude Code failing to launch on macOS 12 (Monterey), a regression introduced in 2.1.255
features.ork_disposition_note: ork declares no macOS version floor and no hook branches on the OS release: grep -rniE "monterey|macos 12|darwin 21" over src shared tests scripts manifests CLAUDE.md = 0 hits; the five process.platform checks in src/hooks/src (notification/desktop.ts, notification/sound.ts, permission-denied/denial-notification.ts, setup/*.ts) pick a notifier by platform, not by version. Nothing to change; users on Monterey regain a binary that starts.

features.description: Remote and scheduled sessions no longer fail with "user messages must have non-empty content" after a re-sent permission approval could not be applied.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed remote and scheduled sessions failing with "user messages must have non-empty content" after a re-sent permission approval could not be applied
features.ork_disposition_note: Free. ork drives no remote (claude.ai Remote Control) or scheduled (cloud routine) sessions: every headless caller in ork is a local `claude -p` (ci-sentinel, claude-triage, claude-health, claude-release-watch, labs-version-watch, skill-eval, plugin-validation workflows; tests/evals/scripts/lib/eval-common.sh), which is a different session type. grep for the error text in src, shared/rules, tests, scripts = 0 relevant hits (three unrelated "non-empty content" strings in analytics docs and a script-structure test).

features.description: Four fixes: macOS 'task output swap refused' Bash failures, always-allow not saving in a project with no settings.local.json yet, Remote Control stalls on degraded connections, oversized background-task failure notifications exceeding the API size limit.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed "always allow" not saving in a project that has no .claude/settings.local.json yet
features.ork_disposition_note: Already recorded as featureless in cc-support.json (2026-09-01 note). No settings keys, hook events, tools or permission surfaces changed.

features.description: claude-fable-5-1 is the default Fable model: 1M context, $10/$50 per MTok, cache reads $0.25/MTok.
features.reference_changelog_line: Added Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`), now the default Fable model — 1M context, $10/$50 per Mtok with $0.25/Mtok cache reads
features.ork_disposition_note: Added to src/hooks/src/lib/models.vocab.json (fullIds + pricing, `fable` alias now resolves to 5.1 like CC does) and tests/ci/claude-model-ids.txt. cost-estimator picks the $0.25 cache-read rate up via the vocab import.

features.description: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE applies CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (or the main model) to every subagent, ignoring per-spawn and agent-definition model overrides.
features.reference_changelog_line: Added `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` to apply `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` (or the main model) to every subagent, ignoring per-spawn and agent-definition model overrides
features.ork_disposition_note: Documented in configure/cc-version-settings.md. DEFERRED (S): fable-spend-consent still prompts on an explicit fable pin that CC will ignore when FORCE is set; add an env short-circuit. The 23 explicit `model:` pins (7 haiku, 10 sonnet, 6 opus) and test-agent-model-tool-correlation.sh stay correct as authoring policy but are inert under FORCE; note that in agent-authoring.md.

features.description: `/effort s` sets effort for the current session only; `--effort` now lifts a new model's default-effort hold per session instead of permanently.
features.reference_changelog_line: Added `s` in `/effort` to change effort for the current session only, matching `/model`
features.ork_disposition_note: Doc note only. Skill-level `effort:` frontmatter is a different mechanism and is untouched.

features.description: Auto mode prompts once before the first file read outside the working directories; permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories blocks such reads.
features.reference_changelog_line: Added a one-time prompt in auto mode before the first file read outside the working directories, with the option to block such reads (`permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`)
features.ork_disposition_note: Documented in configure/cc-version-settings.md. DEFERRED (S): ork skills read ~/.claude (analytics, dream, memory) and cross-repo paths; doctor should warn when the key is true and additionalDirectories does not cover those paths.

features.description: timeFormat and timeZone settings control the turn-end clock and transcript timestamps (12h, 24h, 24h UTC, or strftime).
features.reference_changelog_line: Added "Time format" (`timeFormat`) and `timeZone` settings: 12-hour, 24-hour, 24-hour UTC, or a strftime pattern for the turn-end clock and transcript-view timestamps
features.ork_disposition_note: Documented in configure/cc-version-settings.md. Operator proposal: timeFormat 24h.

features.description: Auto mode no longer auto-approves cloud metadata-credential fetches, egress evasion, or cross-tenant reach unless the environment marks them expected.
features.reference_changelog_line: Added a Containment Escape rule to auto mode so cloud metadata-credential fetches, egress evasion, and cross-tenant reach are no longer auto-approved unless your environment marks them expected
features.ork_disposition_note: network-egress-guard.ts has no metadata-endpoint coverage (grep 169.254 in src/hooks/src: 0 hits). CC now covers it natively in auto mode; per shared/rules/cc-native-first.md do not add a regex twin.

features.description: defaultMode: bypassPermissions in .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json is now ignored (like auto); set it in user or managed settings or pass --permission-mode.
features.reference_changelog_line: Changed `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` to be ignored, like `"auto"`; set it in user or managed settings, or pass `--permission-mode`
features.ork_disposition_note: Documented in configure/cc-version-settings.md. ork's tracked settings set no defaultMode (grep: 0). Users who fled to bypass mode via project settings (08-31 feedback) lose it silently; the doc says where it must live now.

features.description: Worktree-isolated sessions no longer refuse Bash loops, $VAR reads, "$(...)" and heredocs that never touch git as too complex to verify.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed worktree-isolated sessions refusing Bash loops, `$VAR` reads, `"$(…)"` and heredocs that never touch git as "too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree"
features.ork_disposition_note: 25 agents declare `isolation: worktree` (grep src/agents). Free. The cross-repo `git -C` refusal (hq-ext #795) is a different check and is NOT lifted by this bullet.

features.description: Sandboxed git in a linked worktree keeps write access to the common .git directory after cd into a subdirectory.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed sandboxed git commands in a linked worktree losing write access to the repository's common `.git` directory after `cd` into a subdirectory
features.ork_disposition_note: Free. A plausible contributor to the 'worktree operations exit 0 but do nothing' reports in memory; not re-measured here.

features.description: claude -p no longer exits ~5s after its final result while a Monitor the model armed is still running; it waits for the watch to fire or time out.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed `claude -p` exiting about 5 seconds after its final result while a Monitor the model armed was still running; it now waits for the watch to fire or time out
features.ork_disposition_note: Headless callers with an outer timeout (tests/evals/scripts/lib/eval-common.sh run_with_timeout 30; ci-sentinel ORK_SENTINEL_PER_PR_TIMEOUT_S 300) will now hit that timeout if the model arms a Monitor. Watch on the next eval run; no code change yet.

features.description: --disallowedTools and session deny rules survive the first settings reload under allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed `--disallowedTools` and session deny rules being dropped after the first settings reload when `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` is enabled
features.ork_disposition_note: No ork guard depends on the CLI flag; agent frontmatter disallowedTools is a different mechanism. Free.

features.description: Bash Read()/Edit() deny rules now apply to < file redirects and reader commands like tac and egrep.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed Bash `Read()`/`Edit()` deny rules not applying to `< file` redirects and reader commands like `tac` and `egrep`; a deny rule on any argument or redirect target now refuses the command
features.ork_disposition_note: Strengthens the CC-native Read() deny rules that replaced credential-read-guard in purge wave 3 (#3840). Free.

features.description: A permissions.ask rule is no longer skipped in auto mode when the matching command runs inside a compound command or subshell.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed a `permissions.ask` rule being skipped in auto mode when the matching command ran inside a compound command or subshell, letting it run without the confirmation prompt
features.ork_disposition_note: Free; ork ships no permissions.ask rules of its own.

features.description: Bash permission checks no longer auto-approve [[ ]] conditionals that zsh parses differently from bash.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed Bash permission checks auto-approving certain `[[ ]]` conditionals that zsh parses differently from bash; these commands now prompt for approval
features.ork_disposition_note: Free.

features.description: Plugin component paths (command, agent, skill, hooks) that are symlinks are refused, closing reads outside the plugin directory.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed plugins being able to read files outside their own directory through a declared command, agent, skill, hooks or other component path that is a symlink; such paths are now refused with an error
features.ork_disposition_note: plugins/ork contains 0 symlinks (find -type l, VERIFIED). No-op.

features.description: /add-dir accepts a directory inside the cwd and loads its skills, commands and agents like --add-dir does at startup.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed `/add-dir` rejecting a directory inside the current working directory; it now loads that directory's skills, commands, and agents like `--add-dir` does at startup
features.ork_disposition_note: No ork surface depends on it.

features.description: /fork keeps the original conversation's prompt cache in the new background session; the worktree briefing arrives as a message, not a system-prompt change.
features.reference_changelog_line: Improved `/fork` to keep the original conversation's prompt cache in the new background session: its worktree briefing now arrives as a message instead of a system-prompt change
features.ork_disposition_note: Free for the 80 `context: fork` skills.

features.description: Subagents cut off mid-stream (sleep, dropped connection, server error) now continue automatically instead of ending with an incomplete response.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed subagents stopping when a response was cut off mid-stream by a computer sleep, dropped connection, or server error; they now automatically continue instead of ending with an incomplete response
features.ork_disposition_note: subagent-stop/retry-handler.ts is orchestration-level (failed agent, suggest alternative), not a mid-stream retry, so nothing to subtract. Free.

features.description: Background sessions: start during macOS npm self-update, state.json detail, Completed ordering, --bg from a deleted dir, --resume double listing, --continue opens finished sessions, old-binary retirement, agents --json raw-mode fix, stashed prompt kept.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed `claude agents --json` briefly switching the terminal to raw mode and undoing another program's terminal settings on exit
features.ork_disposition_note: Free. ork drives no `claude --bg`; herdr is a separate multiplexer and unaffected.

features.description: Non-JSONL data piped into claude -p --input-format stream-json fails fast instead of growing memory unbounded.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed unbounded memory growth when non-JSONL data is piped into `claude -p --input-format stream-json`; it now fails fast with a clear error
features.ork_disposition_note: eval-common.sh:258 pipes probe input into --input-format stream-json; a malformed probe now errors instead of hanging. Free.

features.description: Gateway-discovered /model entries may carry a description; discovery runs even under CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC; `fable`/`best` keep resolving to Fable 5 on gateways until 5.1 is configured there.
features.reference_changelog_line: Added support for a gateway-supplied `description` on discovered `/model` picker entries (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY`); entries without one still read "From gateway"
features.ork_disposition_note: llm-integration/model-selection.md already documents the discovery env. Note only.

features.description: sandbox.network.deniedDomains entries now block a host written with a trailing dot inside the sandbox.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed sandbox network hosts written with a trailing dot (`example.com.`): a `deniedDomains` entry didn't block the host inside the sandbox, and "don't ask again" for such a host kept prompting
features.ork_disposition_note: Closes a bypass in the deniedDomains rollout (#3322/#3424) that network-egress-guard's retirement is gated on. Free.

features.description: /doctor warns about stale sandbox mask files left by a killed session.
features.reference_changelog_line: Added a `/doctor` warning for stale sandbox mask files left by a killed session
features.ork_disposition_note: CC's /doctor now owns this; ork's sandbox-posture lib does not duplicate it (cc-native-first).

features.description: /code-review --comment posts findings on GitLab merge requests via glab mr note.
features.reference_changelog_line: Improved `/code-review --comment` to post findings on GitLab merge requests via `glab mr note` instead of reporting the target as unsupported
features.ork_disposition_note: One-line note added to review-pr/SKILL.md next to the existing --comment sentence.

features.description: Settings in a .claude/ folder created after startup are picked up without a restart.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed settings in a `.claude/` folder created after startup not being picked up until restart
features.ork_disposition_note: The ConfigChange settings-reload hook now also sees a late-created project settings file. Free.

features.description: Detached background commands (timeout, setsid) no longer survive a task stop or exit; stopping a background subagent stops its monitors; Claude is told when you stop a background command.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed background commands that detach from their shell (for example under `timeout` or `setsid`) surviving a task stop or Claude Code exit
features.ork_disposition_note: Free.

features.description: --add-dir, /add-dir and additionalDirectories refuse UNC shares and /net automounts.
features.reference_changelog_line: Changed `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, and `additionalDirectories` to refuse network paths (UNC shares, `/net/<host>` automounts) with a message before touching them; on Windows use a mapped drive letter
features.ork_disposition_note: No network paths in any ork settings profile.

features.description: Proactive output style sessions idle instead of busy-looping while a background command or Monitor they started is running.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed Proactive output style sessions busy-looping with filler messages and repeated log reads instead of idling while a background command or Monitor they started is still running
features.ork_disposition_note: ork ships no Proactive style.

features.description: /btw history browsing moved from left/right arrows to Shift+arrows or [ ]; Ctrl+E command explanation removed from Bash permission prompts.
features.reference_changelog_line: Changed `/btw` history browsing from `←`/`→` to `Shift+←`/`Shift+→` (or `[`/`]`), stepping through your recent side questions and back to the live answer
features.ork_disposition_note: No ork doc cites the old keys (grep /btw and Ctrl+E: 0 in src).

features.description: managedSourcesBehavior merge takes sandbox.credentials.awsPairs and sandbox.ripgrep whole from the highest source; policyHelper timeouts clamped; shadowed policyHelper runs when the fetch reports removal.
features.reference_changelog_line: Changed `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` to take `sandbox.credentials.awsPairs` and `sandbox.ripgrep` whole from the highest managed source that sets them instead of combining the sources' values
features.ork_disposition_note: No managed settings in the estate.

features.description: Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry header and profile fixes, Remote Control consent and model fixes, gateway TLS pinning, Cowork artifact asks.
features.reference_changelog_line: Fixed dismissing the Remote Control consent prompt (Esc, or `n` at `claude remote-control`) counting as consent, so the next request connected without asking
features.ork_disposition_note: Not a plugin surface.

features.description: VS Code: account/usage headers, model pill with effort row, output style picker, archive sessions, provider-feature gating.
features.reference_changelog_line: [VSCode] Added output style selection to the command menu, including custom styles
features.ork_disposition_note: Not a plugin surface.
